title: Signal
logline: A rooftop sentry robot waits four thousand nights for its maker's signal, until the city goes dark and it must choose what to guard.
look: Rain-soaked pixel city, magenta and cyan neon against deep navy; whole-pixel moves, 8 to 12 fps cycles, hit-stop on every blackout; dawn in pale pink pixels.
narrator: male, middle-aged, low pitch, american accent
Calm noir narrator, low and measured
music: Chiptune arpeggio over a synth pad and rain; each blackout a bit-crushed hit; a single square-wave melody when the window answers.

shots.direction: EWS · slow parallax · fade in — a rain city in pixels; on a rooftop antenna sits a small sentry robot
MS · locked · cut — its single eye scans; the antenna pings (8 fps cycle)
CU · locked · cut — the screen on its chest: WAITING — NIGHT 4000
WS · slow pan · cut — neon signs flicker across the skyline
WS · locked · hit-stop cuts — districts go dark one by one
CU · locked · cut — its battery icon drops to one bar
WS · slow push · cut — across the street, one window still lit: a child holding a toy robot, the lamp flickering
MS · locked · cut — the robot looks at its antenna, then at the window; it decides
WS · tracking down · hit-stop on sparks — it climbs down and plugs its own core cable into the building's line
CU · locked · cut — the window light steadies; the child presses a hand to the glass
MS · locked · cut — the robot's eye dims; the child blinks a toy flashlight at it: short, short, short
EWS · slow pull back · fade out — rain stops; pixel dawn; the robot dark, the little light still blinking at it

narration.text: It was built to wait for one signal.
Then the city began to go dark.
A sentry guards what matters. It just had to decide what that was.
And from the last lit window, someone answered.
It had never been waiting for the sky.
